Frequently asked questions

Short answers to the questions people ask most about SATOM — passwords and sign-in, permissions, what SATOM changes on appliances, data and backups, updates, high availability, the API and the CLI.

Sign-in and accounts#

What is the default admin password?#

There is none. The first admin password is the one typed during installation, or the value of SATOM_ADMIN_PASSWORD; if neither was given, a random password is written to /opt/satom/initial-admin-password (mode 0600, never to a log). See First login and Installation.

How many failed sign-ins lock an account, and for how long?#

10 consecutive failures lock the account for 15 minutes. Separately, each client address may try to sign in 5 times per minute. An administrator can unlock with sudo satom execute admin unlock <username>. See Security model.

Can I use Active Directory, LDAP or RADIUS?#

Yes. Configure the sources in Settings → Authentication. They are tried in the configured order; local accounts always keep working and never fall through to a directory.

Is two-factor authentication supported?#

Yes, TOTP with one-time backup codes, for local accounts. Directory accounts do their MFA at the directory.

Is there an idle session timeout?#

Yes. Settings → General → Session Lock (minutes) (5 to 1440, default 60) is an idle timeout: a browser session with no page load, navigation or form submission for longer than that is signed out on its next request, with "Your session was locked after N minutes of inactivity." Background refreshes such as the notification bell do not keep a session alive. API tokens are not affected. Separately, forms carry a CSRF token valid for one hour; an expired form is simply re-submitted.

How long must a password be?#

12 to 1024 characters, with no character-class rule. The same rule applies on every path that sets a password: Change Password, Add User, administrator reset, the reset link, the CLI and both installers. Existing passwords are not re-checked until they are changed.

ℹ️Note

Changed in 2.11.0: Session Lock is enforced as an idle timeout (before, the setting had no effect), the password minimum is 12 characters everywhere, and the sidebar only shows pages the user can open.

Permissions#

What can the built-in profiles do?#

Profile Can
readonly View every section, change nothing
operator View, plus manage appliances, protection, network, backups, operations and templates, and use Scout, the AI assistant
admin Everything, including users, profiles, the registry and settings

Create your own profiles from granular permissions; see Users and profiles and Permissions.

Why is a menu entry missing for some users?#

The sidebar shows a link only when the user's profile can open that page. Pages that show device content need a read permission (for example protection.view for the FortiWeb protection pages, registry.view for the API Explorer, monitoring.view for Sentinel), and the Global home lists appliances only to holders of appliances.view. The seeded profiles hold every read key.

Why can't some users see an appliance?#

Appliances in maintenance mode are hidden from users without appliances.view_maintenance, and each ADOM only shows its own product's appliances.

Products and appliances#

Which Fortinet products does SATOM manage?#

FortiWeb, FortiADC, FortiAnalyzer, FortiAuthenticator and, read-only since 3.0, FortiGate, each in its own ADOM, plus a Global ADOM that sees all of them. See ADOMs and products.

Does SATOM change an appliance without showing me first?#

Structured configuration writes go through one writer whose default is a dry-run: it computes the request without contacting the appliance. A real apply takes a before/after snapshot and writes change history and an audit entry. Exceptions are tools that are explicitly raw, such as the API-Registry Explorer and the operator console. Destructive actions (firmware upgrade, reboot) need an approved change request inside its window.

Where are appliance passwords stored?#

In the SATOM database, encrypted with the node's FERNET_KEY. Optionally an external vault can hold them instead (Settings → Vault). See Security model.

Do pages read live from the appliance?#

No — pages render from SATOM's local copy of each appliance's configuration. Contacting the appliance is an explicit action (refresh, sync, save).

Operations#

Why does a fresh installation do nothing automatically?#

Scheduled actions are seeded only when the node gets its first appliance (and only if it has no System Automation yet). Before that, or to fill gaps, run sudo satom execute seed actions to see the recommended set (hourly sync, nightly inspection and system backup, monitoring sweeps, reports, Sentinel jobs) and add --yes to create it. See Scheduled actions.

Do scheduled actions run twice in a two-node pair?#

No. The scheduler only fires on the node whose database is the primary; on the standby it waits and checks again every 30 seconds.

A long action is still running — can I close the browser?#

Yes. Device actions run as background jobs on the server; follow them in the Job Manager. Stop and pause take effect at the next safe point.

Data, backups and logs#

What does a system backup contain?#

A pg_dump of the database, the per-device configuration files and versions, the sealed recovery envelope if one exists, and the documentation redaction rules. It never contains FERNET_KEY or the internal CA key. See System backup and Data and storage.

How long are metrics kept?#

396 days, in the node-local metrics store. See Metrics.

Where are the logs?#

Log Location
Web access / errors /var/log/satom/access.log, /var/log/satom/error.log
Application errors (with error references) /opt/satom/data/logs/satom.log
Background services journalctl -u <unit>
Installer /var/log/satom-install.log
User actions Audit log

Updates, HA and installation#

Can I update a node with no Internet access?#

Yes, with a signed offline update package uploaded on the Software Update page or applied with sudo satom execute update package <file> --yes. See Offline updates.

What happens on the standby node?#

Its database is a read-only replica, scheduled actions do not fire, alert notifications are not sent, and data/ is copied from the primary every 5 minutes. Changes must be made on the primary. Failover is manual. See High availability.

Can I run SATOM in Docker?#

Yes. The container stack runs the application, PostgreSQL, Redis, the metrics store and an nginx proxy. Host-level actions (software update, service control, certificate activation, unit health) are refused unless the optional operations agent is enabled. See Installation.

Does the browser need Internet access?#

No. Every script, stylesheet and font is served by the SATOM node; the Content-Security-Policy allows no other origin.

Which languages does the interface support?#

English, Español, Deutsch, Français and Italiano. Each user chooses a language; administrators choose which are offered.

How big should the server be?#

From 2 vCPU / 4 GB / 20 GB for up to 10 appliances to 8 vCPU / 8 GB / 120 GB for about 110. Beyond that, split the fleet across installations. See Installation.

API and CLI#

Is there an API?#

Yes: a token-authenticated REST API at /api/v1, for inventory, triggering non-destructive scheduled actions, firmware checks and WAF/FortiADC carve-outs. It can never upgrade, flash or reboot an appliance. See REST API v1.

Can a token do more than the user who owns it?#

No. A token cannot be created or edited with a scope its owner's permissions do not cover, every call checks that the owner still holds the matching permission, and a disabled owner disables all their tokens.

What is the satom command?#

A console tool on the node for diagnostics, repairs, updates and recovery, which works even when the web interface is down. Read commands work for any user; changes need sudo. See CLI.
